_note: Display values for the Alderbrook Strategy Lab. Every number matches the final 6-slide deck (docs/03_deck_content_final.md). Live simulator values come from engine/engine.py; at default inputs they must equal these.

recommendation.one_liner: Buy 60% of Brightwater at close and the remaining 40% at the end of FY27, priced on audited FY27 revenue. Open at $400M; walk away above $450M.
recommendation.tagline: Buy the engine. Stage the cheque. Pay for proof.

mix.note: 12.0% if Vital grows 7.2% a year on Brightwater's engine

organic_bridge.note: Vital held flat at $22M; rest of hydration/other grows 11%

scorecard_at_ask.npv_note: risk-adjusted for 50% chance of sale after FY27; incl. ~$53.6M terminal value at 8x
scorecard_at_ask.verdict: Plan B only; no brand control

option_rationales.Brightwater 60% / 40%: Only path that passes growth, leverage and margin together, buys a 90-day innovation engine and 5 AI specialists, and pays the second 40% only for proven FY27 revenue.
option_rationales.Brightwater 100% now: Same assets, but all risk paid up front: leverage hits 3.04x, above the board's 2.5x.
option_rationales.Marrow Lane 100%: Profitable cold brew (~$81M by FY29) but no functional brand, founders exit with no successor, and growth stays at 3.3%.
option_rationales.Distribution partnership: Cheaper up front, but buys no brand and no capability, ends if Brightwater is sold to a rival, and passes only 1 of 4 tests.
option_rationales.Vital relaunch: $50M to retry a brand at $22M revenue, 60% sold on promotion, with the same 14-month innovation cycle.

deal.tranche2_formula: 40% x MIN($450M, 2.75 x audited FY27 revenue), paid at end of FY27

stress_at_ask.change: Only 50% of cost of goods eligible for savings
stress_at_ask.meaning: Audit co-packer cost buckets, changeover and transfer costs.
Staging is not cheaper if the seller charges for waiting.
Also lifts leverage to 2.52x at the ask (2.41x at $400M).

prior_acquisitions: 2016 and 2019 ($40M and $65M): both brands now below acquisition-year revenue (case p.4)
